title: Marijuana Is In Schedule One. Fentanyl Is In Schedule 2. Think About It.

content_html_sanitized:
In 1986, William F. Buckley’s National Review published an article I wrote, HOW THE NARCS CREATED CRACK. To my amazement, someone paid attention to something I wrote, and a number of real economists wrote about it.

 

The Iron law of prohibition is a term I coined… in 1986 which posits that as law enforcement becomes more intense, the potency of prohibited substances increases,  "the harder the enforcement, the harder the drugs."

 

I was right about how prohibition works, but what I did not foresee was that, unlike crack, the “ultimate” drug that killed more than any of the others (other than alcohol and tobacco, of course) would actually come out of the pharmaceutical industry. It is called Fentanyl, and is sold under the brand names, Actiq, Duragesic, and Sublimaze, among others. And before that, there was OxyContin or OxyCodone.

 

Why is this important? Because they officially have a medical use, while cannabis does not. So Fentanyl is in Schedule 2, along with morphine, opium, codeine, and hydrocodone, etc and can be legally prescribed.

 

“Schedule II medications may not be refilled; a new prescription must be written every time.

 

“Medications classified as Schedule III or IV controlled substances may be refilled up to 5 times in a 6-month period.” That is how Biden sort of, kind of, almost maybe thought cannabis should be treated.

 

In 2022, fentanyl was responsible for 200 deaths every day.

See Are fentanyl overdose deaths rising in the US?

Over a quarter of a million Americans have died from a fentanyl overdose since 2018. Of course, that doesn’t mean that all of these deaths came from pharmaceutical Fentanyl. Not at all.

 

“NIH-supported study highlights increasingly dangerous illicit drug supply, risk of pills not coming from a pharmacy.”

 

When I proposed the “Iron Law”, I blamed excessive law enforcement, but the situation with Fentanyl was different. Yes, the War on Drugs had long been aimed at heroin and other opiates, but Fentanyl, like OxyContin, began as a pharmaceutical product that leaked out of the medical system. Fentanyl is around 100 times stronger than morphine or about 50 times stronger than heroin – so the difference between a dose and an overdose is very small.

Well, of course they say that it has “medical” uses because they say that it has medical uses.  And if they say it doesn’t, then it doesn’t until they say it does.

 

In any case, a drug that has killed hundreds of thousands of Americans is listed in Schedule 2, but cannabis, which has no known lethal dose, is listed in Schedule 1. So what is the risk? The risk is not medical. It is political.

See Marinol Was The First Schedule 2 Drug To Be "Down-Scheduled," Boasts Roxanne On Its New Marinol.com Web Site. Doesn’t That Mean That It Should Never Have Been Schedule 2 Anyway?

 

Of course, cannabis has been used medically for thousands of years, and in 1937 the American Medical Association actually opposed the “Marihuana Tax Act”, pointing out its history of medical use. And what was the research and when were the hearings that preceded its removal from the pharmacopoeia? Never. None. Nada.

 

And what was the research and when were the hearings that preceded its being put in Schedule 1?? Never. None. Nada?

 

Was it put there by Richard Nixon’s Surgeon General??? No, by his Attorney General, John Mitchell, who went to prison for his role in the Watergate scandal.

 

So, it was taken out of medical use without any research, and put in Schedule 1, without any research, but moving it to any other Schedule may be political, but it is not medical or scientific.

 

As of August 19, 2019, AMA applauds Surgeon General’s advisory on cannabis. Of course, the “American Medical Association” no longer opposes taking medical marijuana out of Schedule 1, without any evidence, but they also are in favor of keeping it in Schedule 1, until the government agrees to allow research that it should never have been taken out of the pharmacopoeia in the first place.

 

From 1998 DEA FINALLY CONFIRMS THE EXISTENCE OF SUFFICIENT GROUNDS TO REMOVE MARIJUANA FROM HARD DRUGS SCHEDULE OF CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES

 

Oops! How time flies when you’re not in pain or you’re not in prison.

 

Now about that research. It has been used medically for thousands of years and it is currently being used medically by millions of people in the United States and Canada and The Netherlands and Uruguay, etc with no reported deaths, unlike Aspirin, etc.

So, just what kind of research would that august scientific body need to see before it would agree to take cannabis out of the criminal codes and put it back in the medical books?

They have not said. They don’t want to get involved. They’re just passing through town.

Let me make something very clear. I know many chronic pain patients who find cannabis helpful, but the sort of pain treated with Fentanyl, etc, is much more severe. I do not know if cannabis could be helpful in such extreme conditions. That is not my point.

But I do know that patients should be free to try it in whatever circumstances. I also know that official medicine does not know if cannabis will help their patients, because they will not even look. I also know that official medicine has turned its back on their patients who benefited from cannabis when they used it despite the opposition from official medical.

While law enforcement did indeed make the drug problem worse in many ways. Official medicine has betrayed both their patients and medical science.
